Incumbent [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] [[Jan Brewer]] ran for a full term. Brewer ascended to the governorship following the resignation of the incumbent [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] Governor [[Janet Napolitano]] to become [[United States Secretary of Homeland Security|secretary of Homeland Security]] in the [[Obama administration|Obama Administration]]. Primaries were held on August 24, 2010. Brewer won a full term, defeating [[Arizona Attorney General]] and Democratic nominee [[Terry Goddard]] 54% to 42%. ==Background== [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] [[Governor of Arizona|Governor]] [[Janet Napolitano]] was [[Term limits in the United States|term-limited]] and nominated to become [[secretary of Homeland Security]] by [[President-elect of the United States|President-elect]] [[Barack Obama]], and was confirmed by the [[United States Senate]] on January 20, 2009, resigning as governor the same day.{{cite web |title=Governor: Napolitano resigns |url=http://www.arizonaguardian.com/azg/index.php?option=com_content&view=category&layout=blog&id=35&Itemid=58&limitstart=125 |publisher=The Arizona Guardian |date=January 20, 2009 |access-date=September 2, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110721131443/http://www.arizonaguardian.com/azg/index.php?option=com_content&view=category&layout=blog&id=35&Itemid=58&limitstart=125 |archive-date=July 21, 2011 |url-status=dead |df=mdy-all }} Since Arizona does not have a [[Lieutenant governor (United States)|lieutenant governor]], [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] [[Secretary of State of Arizona|Secretary of State]] [[Jan Brewer]] was first in the state's gubernatorial line of succession and was sworn in as governor upon Napolitano's resignation. Brewer announced on November 5, 2009, that she would seek a full term in 2010.{{cite news |title= Brewer running for full term as Ariz. governor |first= Paul |last= Davenport |newspaper= [[The Arizona
